en: The Rafflesia schadenbergiana is a rare parasitic plant in the Philippines that produces the largest flowers but lacks true leaves, stems, or roots.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle hunts flying lemurs and has a distinctive shaggy crest of brown feathers on its head.
National Scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator to provide affordable healthcare for newborn babies in rural areas.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary in the Sulu Sea that houses hundreds of coral and fish species.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are larger than its brain and can rotate its head one hundred eighty degrees.
The dugong is a marine mammal found in Palawan that grazes on seagrass and is closely related to the manatee.
The Rhizophora mangrove tree survives in salty coastal ecosystems by using specialized stilt roots to absorb oxygen directly from the air.
The whale shark is the largest fish in the ocean and uses its massive mouth to filter-feed on tiny plankton.
The islets of Langerhans are specific cell clusters in the human pancreas that produce insulin to regulate blood sugar.
The Cavendish banana plant reproduces asexually by growing new shoots from an underground stem structure called a corm.
The tamaraw is a small, endangered, hoofed mammal with V-shaped horns that is found exclusively on the island of Mindoro.
Mount Apo is a protected natural park in Mindanao that provides a critical highland habitat for the endemic Philippine eagle.
